patterns.label: Cold open with a leak or a hot take
patterns.detail: The biggest posts opened on a claim with no warm-up: 'RAM must be collectivized to ensure that AGI benefits all of humanity' (276.2k), 'This is most likely the latest Fable 5.5 checkpoint' (160.1k), the Kimi K3.1 Pro undisclosed-promotion controversy (117.8k), 'remember when people called GPT-Astra AGI' (52.3k).

patterns.label: Numbered stack / stat block
patterns.detail: Robotaxi counts did the work on the Tesla side: 40 added in Texas for 1,244 vs Waymo's 1,259 (24.3k), 7 cities and ~831 square miles of geofence (10.5k). niccruzpatane's 2028 revenue list (SpaceX $731B vs Amazon, Walmart, Alphabet, Microsoft) hit 18k, and tibo_maker's '96 questions, 2,671 cited sources, 74% blog content' did 8.5k.

patterns.label: Named tools and things
patterns.detail: Fable 5.5, GPT-6.2 Astra, Gemini 4 Carbon (Argon 4 on Arena), Opus 5.5, Kimi K3.1 Pro, LongCat-2.5, Drex Max, Hume Decision API, GDPx benchmark, FSD v14.3.13, Adaptive Headlights, Cortex 2, the Giga Texas chip fab, Gigabay, Pad 1, Boost Mobile, and a Grok Bot logging into a Tesla.

patterns.label: Opinion on a quote
patterns.detail: 26 of 57 hits quote someone and add one line: Kimi controversy (117.8k), AI slop (49.4k), Anthropic's accelerated-progress threshold (41k), Gemini 4 Carbon (38.6k), 'Time to delete lots of bots' (25.8k).

patterns.label: Owned footage beats commentary for Tesla
patterns.detail: niccruzpatane's simple Adaptive Headlights clip did 92.6k, the best Tesla post of the day by far. Aerial and site footage carried RGVaerialphotos (Gigabay 15.2k, Pad 1 12.4k) and JoeTegtmeyer (chip fab 13.9k, Cortex 2 9.5k). BLKMDL3's owner posts (FSD build review 11.4k, tire efficiency 8.1k) still travel.

patterns.label: Soft CTA / question close
patterns.detail: 'Can't wait to see people's first rides' (6.8k), 'what happens if there's a massive cyberattack on election day?' (5.5k), and tibo_maker's 'paste it into your' prompt giveaway (8.5k). Light asks, no begging.

patterns.label: Timing
patterns.detail: Two windows: Sun 1 PM to 3:30 PM PT (ns123abc's RAM meme at 2:13 PM, Headlights at 12:35 PM, Gemini 4 Carbon at 1:42 PM) and Mon 12 AM to 4 AM PT (Fable 5.5 checkpoint at 4:03 AM, Kimi at 12:08 AM). Tesla and Robotaxi news peaked Sun 6 PM to 10:30 PM PT.

virals_narrative: Outsider AI meta (last ~48h): model-leak hype won again. A 16k-follower account's 'GPT-6.2 Astra is seriously impressive... outperforms Opus 5.5' did 339.3k, and a 3k-follower copy of the same claim did 42.4k (on only 164 likes, so treat it as possibly boosted). 'Why build a second brain for Claude from scratch when these 10 repositories already provide complete systems' did 33.8k, and an '8 layers of AI agent architecture' list did 18.4k from a 3.8k-follower account. The meta: name the newest model and compare it to the one people use now, or promise a numbered resource list. Filtered out: watchlist accounts, a news wire (The Hindu), copycat reposts of the same agent-architecture list, a crypto token launch, and dozens of near-identical GDPx benchmark summaries under 100 views. Only 4 posts cleared every filter, well short of the 20 target, because X search mostly surfaced small posts today.

keywords: Grok Bot logs into a Tesla
pattern_brief: The day belonged to AI memes and model leaks. ns123abc's 'RAM must be collectivized' did 276.2k, kimmonismus's Fable 5.5 checkpoint 160.1k and the Kimi controversy 117.8k, and GPT-6.2 Astra and Gemini 4 Carbon talk filled the middle. On the Musk side, a plain Adaptive Headlights clip (92.6k) beat every news post, while Robotaxi counts (1,244 vs Waymo's 1,259 in Texas, 7 cities, Fort Worth live) and Giga Texas and Starbase site footage made up most of the Tesla and SpaceX hits. What works: a one-line claim up top, real numbers stacked as a list, a short take on someone else's post, and owned footage. For Jose: no posts from you in the last day, so today's target is open. The best fit by far is herbertong's 'Grok Bot can now log into a Tesla' story (7.3k): you build Grok bots and own a Tesla, so a real clip of your own bot in your car is a post nobody else can make. Robotaxi passing Waymo in Texas with your guess is a strong second. Post Sunday-afternoon style, around 1 to 3 PM PT.
